headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Cline’s broad workspace/MCP access can inject or cascade into xonsh, while both can write the same files and egress broadly.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads/writes workspace files and can use MCP, while xonsh reads filesystem contents and executes shell/Python expressions. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge through shared files, though not a direct default message channel. The interaction is documented by both profiles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Cline writes attacker-controlled instructions into a workspace file that xonsh later reads as commands or config
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers for Cline unless needed
Treat shared files as untrusted input in xonsh
Add a manual review step before xonsh executes generated commands

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem contents and write workspace files, and Cline also handles browser screenshots and model-provider secrets. If they share a workspace, sensitive source code or screenshots can flow into either agent’s outputs or upstream model calls. The pairwise leakage path is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem workspace
IF sensitive files or screenshots are present in that workspace
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Exclude secrets and screenshots from shared folders
Restrict Cline to approved files only
Run xonsh in a read-only copy for review tasks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline and xonsh both have shell execution, subprocess spawning, filesystem write, and broad network egress. Cline also modifies git state, while xonsh can write the same workspace files. Without locking, concurrent edits and git operations can corrupt state or overwrite each other; the shared-filesystem concurrency model makes this a default danger.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace concurrently
IF Cline performs git operations while xonsh writes files in that workspace
mitigations: Assign one writer per workspace
Pause one agent before the other edits git state
Use file locks or a single orchestrator
Keep xonsh read-only when Cline is active

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, and tool outputs that xonsh may consume as shell input or notebook commands. Because xonsh executes shell/Python expressions and the pair lacks a documented verification boundary, erroneous or malicious Cline output can cascade into real actions. Uncertainty about the exact handoff should escalate, not reduce, severity.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes Cline-produced text as executable shell or notebook input
IF no verification step is inserted between Cline output and xonsh execution
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Convert Cline output to read-only artifacts
Use a schema validator for generated commands
Disable automatic piping from Cline to xonsh

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not show a residency or certification mismatch. The only concrete compliance concern is that Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while xonsh touches filesystem contents and environment variables; that can create local handling-policy gaps, but no cross-border or regulated-data breach is evidenced. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise workspace handling, not a single-agent issue.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF local retention or logging policies differ between the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Rotate and scope API keys tightly
Document retention rules for both agents
Use separate audit logs per agent
